questions.text: Which JavaScript keyword is block-scoped AND cannot be reassigned?
questions.hint: Think about which keyword is used for values that should never change after declaration.

questions.text: What does typeof null return in JavaScript?
questions.hint: This is a well-known historical bug in JavaScript that was never fixed for backward compatibility.

questions.text: What is a closure in JavaScript?
options: A function that calls itself recursively
A function that remembers variables from its outer scope after that scope has closed
A method for closing a file stream
An error thrown when a variable is out of scope
questions.hint: Think about what happens to the outer function's variables when an inner function is returned.

questions.text: Which of the following is a falsy value in JavaScript?
questions.hint: Remember the six falsy values: false, 0, "", null, undefined, and one more mathematical concept.

questions.text: Which async pattern is considered the cleanest, built on top of Promises?
questions.hint: This pattern lets you write async code that reads almost like synchronous code using two keywords.

questions.text: What does path.basename("/home/user/app/index.js") return?
questions.hint: basename returns the last portion of a file path — including the file extension.

questions.text: In the Node.js event loop, microtasks (Promises, nextTick) run:
options: Between each phase, before the next phase starts
questions.hint: Microtasks always drain completely before the event loop can advance to its next phase.

questions.text: Which runs first among the three?
questions.hint: Order from fastest to slowest: one of these runs before microtasks, one after I/O, one in the timers phase.

questions.text: What does process.argv[0] contain in a Node.js CLI script?
questions.hint: argv[0] and argv[1] are reserved by Node itself — your arguments only start from argv[2].

questions.text: An operational error is best defined as:
options: A bug introduced by the programmer
An expected failure such as a missing file or invalid user input
A crash in the V8 engine
An error that always kills the process
questions.hint: Operational errors are things you anticipate happening in production — not bugs in your code.

questions.text: What HTTP status code means the client is authenticated but NOT permitted to access the resource?
questions.hint: 401 means you're not logged in. This code means you ARE logged in, but you still can't go in.

questions.text: A request has valid syntax but its data fails validation rules. Which status code fits best?
questions.hint: 400 is malformed. This code means the structure is fine, but the business logic rejects the values.

questions.text: What problem do Streams solve that fs.readFile does not?
options: Streams process data in chunks — memory stays flat regardless of file size
questions.hint: Think about what happens to RAM when you load a 2GB file entirely before processing it.

questions.text: Which stream type reads input, transforms it, and passes the result downstream?
questions.hint: Think uppercase converter or gzip compressor — it receives data, modifies it, and outputs a new form.

questions.text: Why should secrets and config NOT be hardcoded in source code?
options: They get committed to version control and become exposed to anyone with access
Hardcoded values are slower to read
npm disallows them in package scripts
questions.hint: Think about what happens when you push your code to GitHub with a database password in it.
